s1.syndrome_frame: A man in his 30s with a left cervical lesion and subsequent lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension and locoregional recurrence with skin metastasis
salient_findings: Lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 30s
Patient has phototype 3 skin
Patient has occupational sun exposure
Patient has fewer than 50 nevi
Initial lesion had Breslow depth of 2.6 mm
Initial lesion had no ulceration
Initial lesion had 7 mitoses/mm2
Patient is BRAF V600E mutation positive
Initial staging CT scan, ultrasonography, lactate dehydrogenase and S-100 protein levels were normal
Selective sentinel node biopsy findings were negative

shortlist.label: Malignant Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: BRAF V600E mutation positive and histopathological study showing infiltrating melanoma

shortlist.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has occupational sun exposure and phototype 3 skin, increasing risk

shortlist.label: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension and locoregional recurrence

shortlist.label: Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has phototype 3 skin and occupational sun exposure, increasing risk

raw.rationale: The patient's initial lesion had a Breslow depth of 2.6 mm, 7 mitoses/mm2, and was BRAF V600E mutation positive, which are all characteristic of malignant melanoma. Additionally, the patient developed lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension and skin metastasis, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's lesion characteristics and BRAF V600E mutation are not typical of squamous cell carcinoma

rejected.label: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's age and lesion characteristics are not typical of Merkel cell carcinoma

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's initial lesion was a solid tumor, not a lymphoid lesion, and the BRAF V600E mutation is not typically associated with lymphoma

rejected.label: Basal Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's lesion characteristics, including the Breslow depth and mitoses/mm2, are not typical of basal cell carcinoma
